newsitem.title: CANADA: Philip, Serv-Tech agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Philip, Serv-Tech agree to merge.

text.p: Philip Environmental Inc and Serv-Tech Inc said on Thursday they signed a definitive merger agreement whereby each share of Serv-Tech stock will be exchanged for 0.403 shares of Philip.

Based on the closing price of Philip Environmental stock on March 5 each Serv-Tech shares is valued at US$6.60. In aggregate, the deal is valued at about US$72 million, including the assumption of about US$21 million of indebtedness.
Philip said the deal is expected to be accretive to Philip's earnings. Closing of the transaction is subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close by June 30.

In 1996, Serv-Tech generated revenue in excess of US$140 million and provided industrial and environmental services from 20 operations, primarily situated in the Gulf Coast region of the United States.

"The merger with Serv-Tech strengthens our presence in the heavily industrialized Gulf Coast region and our services to the hydrocarbon processing industry, a significant market for our integrated services," said Philip President and Chief Executive Allen Fracassi.

"We intend to utilize the strength of our combined management and employee base to integrate Serv-Tech's business and client base with those of Philip in order to facilitate cross-selling of our services into new markets," he added.

Serv-Tech Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Cresci said the merger will facilitate Serv-Tech's expansion into new market sectors serviced by Philip while providing its customers with a broader range of services.

"The merger with Philip provides Serv-Tech's shareholders with the opportunity to participate in the growth of the industrial services market as part of a larger company with a proven track record of success," Cresci said.
